title: Action `visible` CEL cannot see the caller's object permissions — a custom action replacing a built-in CRUD button has no way to express the gate it replaced
body:
## Summary

A custom action's `visible` CEL predicate cannot see the caller's **object-level permissions**. The predicate scope carries identity (`id/name/email/role/roles/isPlatformAdmin/positions`) but nothing from `/auth/me/permissions`, so an author cannot write the one gate they most often want:

```ts
visible: P`current_user.can('my_object', 'delete')`   // no such binding today
```

The consequence shows up as soon as an app replaces a built-in CRUD button with a custom action — the ordinary shape for a **logical delete** (archive / set `status = 'void'` instead of a hard delete). Doing that means `userActions: { delete: false }` plus a custom `…_logical_delete` action, and at that moment the object's `allowDelete` stops governing the button: the built-in gate no longer applies, and the replacement has no way to express the same condition. The button stays visible for accounts with no write grant; the server correctly answers 403, so it is a UI-only leak — but the affordance is there and users click it.

## Where

`app-shell/src/console/AppContent.tsx:679-699` builds the object every action predicate is evaluated against:

```ts
const expressionUser = user ? {
  id, name, email,
  role: user.role ?? 'user',
  roles: (user as any).roles,
  isPlatformAdmin: (user as any).isPlatformAdmin ?? false,
  positions: (user as any).positions ?? [],
} : { name: 'Anonymous', … };
```

`ExpressionProvider` (`providers/ExpressionProvider.tsx:60-72`) then binds it as `current_user` / `user` / `ctx.user` / `os.user` — four aliases of the same permission-free object. Both surfaces the predicate reaches (the toolbar `DeclaredActionsBar` and the row/detail action menus) evaluate against this scope.

The data itself is already in the client: `MePermissionsProvider` holds the full `/auth/me/permissions` payload (`objects[name] = { allowCreate, allowRead, allowEdit, allowDelete, … }`) and exposes `usePermissions().can(object, verb)` — the very verdict the built-in row/toolbar/bulk gates use (objectui#4096). It is simply not wired into the predicate scope.

## Why it matters

Today the only way to gate a custom action on authorization is `requiredPermissions` — a **capability** name (ADR-0066 D4), verified working on both the row menu and the detail header. But a capability is a new authorization concept that has to be declared, granted to every affected audience, and maintained. When all the author wanted was "same rule as the built-in Delete this action replaces", minting a parallel capability is a change to the app's permission model — reviewers rightly stop and ask whether the two can drift apart. That is a real cost paid for a missing binding, and the alternative authors reach for instead (hard-coding role or account names into metadata) is exactly what should stay impossible.

## Ask

Bind the caller's effective object permissions into the predicate scope, so `visible` / `disabled` can express the same verdict the built-in affordances already compute. Either shape works:

* a map — `current_user.permissions['my_object'].allowDelete`, mirroring the `/auth/me/permissions` payload; or
* a function — `current_user.can('my_object', 'delete')`, mirroring `usePermissions().can` and reading better in CEL.

Two things worth deciding alongside:

1. **Fail direction.** Predicates default to *visible* when the scope has not loaded (`ExpressionProvider` doc-comment). A permission-shaped binding wants the opposite for the unloaded case, or a leak reappears on first paint.
2. **Server parity.** The `current_user` / `os.user` aliases exist so a predicate evaluates identically on client, server-formula and server-RLS (ADR-0068). A new sub-object should either be honoured on the server paths too or be explicitly documented as client-only UI gating — a binding that silently means different things on the two ends is worse than none.

## Evidence

Found while investigating an app whose logical-delete action stayed visible for a no-write-grant account: the built-in row **Edit** correctly disappeared for that account (objectui#4096 working as intended), while the custom **Delete** replacing the built-in one remained on both the row menu and the detail header. The app then verified that `requiredPermissions` does gate the action on both surfaces — so the gap is specifically that the *permission verdict* is unreachable from CEL, not that the action is ungateable.
